name: game-network-a1
description: Step A1 of docs/design/game-reconstruction-and-motion.md, for a GPU that runs the guest's tensor instructions through shared memory: an Intel GPU whose driver lists an 8x16x16 fp16 shape (Xe2: Arc 140V, B580), or an AMD RDNA 3 GPU (16x16x16, where only EDEN_NX2_HMMA_ZERO_C applies). Not the Arc 140T: its driver lists 8x8x16 with fp32 accumulators only, so every variant there runs in software and the EDEN_NX2_TENSOR_LOG lines say so. Ocarina of Time's own network with EDEN_NX2_INTEL_COOP_MATRIX=1 in every variant (the suite's baseline 'coop'), then with each switch that cuts the shared-memory traffic around a tensor operation (EDEN_NX2_HMMA_ZERO_C, bit-exact; EDEN_NX2_HMMA_K16_ONCE, which rounds once per K=16) and with both. The network runs in every variant: game presets off, anti-aliasing Game, frame generation off, the Max Resolution add-on on (its default). The cost to compare is the output pass's GPU time in each row's gpu_costs (work, shader 6bd913e1f34e83eb). A row counts only when its log has the EDEN_NX2_TENSOR_LOG line for that shader with cooperative matrices and no 'anti-aliasing network bypassed' line. Every arm translates the network afresh: run the suite twice in one session and read only the second pass, comparing its two coop rows first.
